symptoms.symptom: ros2 topic list shows nothing from /talos, only /parameter_events and /rosout
symptoms.cause: Your shell isn't on Zenoh, or it can't reach the router on the Orin. The team's client config connects to tcp/orin2:7447, so orin2 must resolve on your machine. The ros2 daemon may also still hold the RMW from before you sourced.
symptoms.check: echo $RMW_IMPLEMENTATION must say rmw_zenoh_cpp (the rmw alias prints the team setting). ping orin2. Then ros2 topic list --no-daemon.

symptoms.symptom: Everyone loses the robot at once; the launcher page says Discovery: Self Hosted (CRASHED!)
symptoms.cause: The launcher runs the Zenoh router (rmw_zenohd) itself. If the router exits, the launcher logs its output and stops, and systemd restarts the whole service, which stops every launch.
symptoms.check: journalctl -u ros_launcher -n 100 on the Orin: look for Zenoh Router Died! and the router's stderr just after it.

symptoms.symptom: ros2 topic echo says the message type is invalid; the viewer's plot row says Can't read this topic
symptoms.cause: The message type (usually a riptide_msgs2 one) isn't installed in your shell: only /opt/ros is sourced.
symptoms.check: source ~/osu-uwrt/release/install/setup.bash, then start the tool (or the viewer) again from that shell.

symptoms.symptom: ros2 topic hz on a laptop says a camera stream is slow
symptoms.cause: A rate measured on a laptop is the rate that crossed the tether or Wi-Fi, not what the Orin publishes. Subscribing to several camera streams at once loads the link further.
symptoms.check: Measure one topic at a time. For the true rate, run ros2 topic hz on the Orin over SSH.

src.label: pretest_checks: rates measured one topic at a time

symptoms.symptom: The launcher page at http://orin2:8080 doesn't load
symptoms.cause: ros_launcher.service is down or restarting. It restarts 0.5 s after any exit, but systemd gives up if it fails 5 times in 15 s.
symptoms.check: systemctl status ros_launcher (its status line names the launch file and how many launches are active), then journalctl -u ros_launcher -n 100.

symptoms.symptom: A launch sits at 3/4 completed on the launcher page instead of Running
symptoms.cause: The launcher counts a launch as running once every topic listed for it in the launch YAML has been seen. One hasn't: that node didn't start, or the topic was renamed. Hover the bar for Pending Topics. riptide_navigation's entry lists /a.
symptoms.check: Read the launch's output on the launcher page (cyan while starting). The page shows only lines printed while it is open: for earlier ones, restart the launch with the page open, or read ~/.ros/log/ on the Orin. ros2 topic hz on the pending topic.

symptoms.symptom: A launch's bar on the launcher page says ERROR!
symptoms.cause: Its ros2 launch process exited (a node crashed with the launch, or a monitored topic's monitor died). The launcher logs Launch died and stops the rest of it.
symptoms.check: If the launcher page was open when it died, its output shows the crash; the page keeps nothing, so otherwise read ~/.ros/log/ on the Orin, or restart the launch with the page open. The launcher's own log: journalctl -u ros_launcher --since "10 min ago".

symptoms.symptom: ZED topics missing or camera frames not in TF, with the bench launch file loaded
symptoms.cause: talos_launch_bench_mpc.yaml lists two navigation.launch.py entries. The cameras need riptide_hardware2's one, which publishes the robot model and both ZED camera frames, running alongside zed.launch.py. riptide_navigation's (mode:=replacement) is the other one.
symptoms.check: On the launcher page, check the package under the running navigation.launch.py. ros2 run tf2_ros tf2_echo talos/base_link talos/ffc_camera_link.

symptoms.symptom: The launcher page lists Abandoned Launches or Orphans
symptoms.cause: You loaded another launch file while launches were running (they become zombies and are asked to stop), or processes escaped a launch's shutdown. Orphans can keep publishing and confuse everything after.
symptoms.check: systemctl status ros_launcher says "N Launches Active; M Abandoned". Stop launches before loading a new file. As a last resort, sudo systemctl restart ros_launcher stops every node.

symptoms.symptom: No state/firmware, no depth, no thruster telemetry
symptoms.cause: The CAN side is down: the hardware launch (it runs the micro-ROS agent for the boards) isn't running, can0 is down, or a board is unpowered.
symptoms.check: ros2 topic echo /talos/state/firmware --field board_name should list every board within a few seconds. On the Orin: ip -br link show can0, then candump can0 for the boards' own frames (see Firmware).

symptoms.symptom: dvl_twist stops; MPC warns Stale sensors, using EKF instead: dvl
symptoms.cause: The DVL lost bottom lock (too close to the floor, beams on a wall, bubbles, out of the water). The driver only publishes dvl_twist when the velocity is valid, and the MPC calls the DVL stale after 1 s. On the DvlWaterTrackFallback branch the water-track velocity goes to dvl/water_twist, but nothing uses it yet: it is relative to the water, not the floor.
symptoms.check: ros2 topic echo /talos/dvl/bottom_lock; ros2 topic hz /talos/dvl_twist (8 Hz when locked).

symptoms.symptom: DVL velocities about 1 % off, or it stops measuring after you poked at it
symptoms.cause: Its settings changed (speed of sound 1480 m/s fixed, 8 Hz, water track on). Connecting to ports 9000/9001 is the command interface and stops the measurement.
symptoms.check: Read the settings from the DVL's web page, Measurement Configuration, at 192.168.1.212. Don't open 9000/9001 just to look.

symptoms.symptom: On the bench, dvl_twist runs at 8 Hz but only ever reads near zero, and every DVL beam is valid
symptoms.cause: Expected with the bench launch file. talos_launch_bench_mpc.yaml starts hardware_fake_dvl.launch.py, which runs fake_dvl.py instead of the DVL driver: zero velocity plus 5 mm/s of random noise, every beam flagged valid, stamped as it is sent (not back-dated).
symptoms.check: On the launcher page, see which hardware launch is loaded: hardware.launch.py (pool file talos_launch_mpc.yaml) runs the real DVL. ros2 node list | grep fake_dvl.

symptoms.symptom: EKF velocity trails the DVL by 0.2–0.35 s; roll and pitch rates are small and late
symptoms.cause: The IMU reports angular_velocity_covariance 0.01, but its measured still noise is about 1e-6, so the EKF hardly trusts it: rates lag the IMU by ~455 ms at 12–15 % of their size. DVL messages arrive ~125 ms after their stamp and smooth_lagged_data is off. The MPC's own estimator is on time; mapping's motion model uses the EKF.
symptoms.check: Record the IMU, FOG, DVL, depth and odometry/filtered, then cross-correlate (or replay the EKF, below).

symptoms.symptom: Talos sits still on the bench but its pose creeps
symptoms.cause: Usually heading: an old or bad FOG tare. The pre-test limits are 1 m per hour of position drift and 0.5° per minute of yaw.
symptoms.check: Watch odometry/filtered for a minute. Tare only with Talos still on a level surface: ros2 action send_goal /talos/gyro/tare riptide_msgs2/action/TareGyro "{num_samples: 100000, timeout_seconds: 20}"

symptoms.symptom: MPC log: <frame> mount in the vehicle YAML differs from TF by … deg / … cm
symptoms.cause: The vehicle YAML the MPC loads and the URDF behind TF disagree about where a sensor sits. One of them was edited.
symptoms.check: ros2 run tf2_ros tf2_echo talos/base_link talos/imu_link, compared with riptide_descriptions/config/talos.yaml.

symptoms.symptom: Enabled, but the thrusters do nothing for about 5 seconds
symptoms.cause: Normal. A kill cuts ESC power; when power returns the ESC boards hold ESC_POWERON_DELAY for 5000 ms while the ESCs start up, and the overseer keeps motion_enabled false.
symptoms.check: ros2 topic echo /talos/state/thrusters/telemetry --no-arr: disabled_flags bit 2 (value 4) is the power-on delay and clears by itself. Telemetry alternates between the two ESC boards (start_thruster_num 0 and 4): read both.

symptoms.symptom: Thrusters stop mid-run; telemetry shows TGT_RPM_STALE, then TGT_RPM_STALE_PENALTY
symptoms.cause: No RPM command reached the ESC board for 500 ms while the thrusters were spinning. The board raises a fault and refuses commands for 1 s more. The controller stopped, stalled or lost CAN.
symptoms.check: The MPC's log for CAN thruster command failed (the direct sign) or MPC failed. ros2 topic hz /talos/command/requested_rpm (20 Hz) only shows the MPC is ticking: it is a copy of what goes over CAN. candump can0 on the Orin shows the frames themselves (Firmware).

symptoms.symptom: MPC log: No fresh odometry; thrusters off
symptoms.cause: The newest odometry/filtered is more than 0.5 s old, judged by its header stamp against the MPC's clock. The EKF stopped, or the two run on machines whose clocks disagree.
symptoms.check: ros2 topic hz /talos/odometry/filtered (30 Hz). If the MPC isn't on the Orin, compare clocks (chronyc tracking).

symptoms.symptom: MPC log: Stale sensors, using EKF instead: gyro fog dvl
symptoms.cause: The listed channels went quiet longer than their timeouts (gyro 0.2 s, FOG 0.1 s, IMU orientation 0.5 s, DVL 1.0 s, depth 0.5 s), so the MPC's estimator borrows the EKF for them. Only dvl is routine (bottom lock).
symptoms.check: ros2 topic hz on each named topic.

symptoms.symptom: MPC runs and publishes thruster_forces, but the ESCs never get RPM
symptoms.cause: Hardware output is off. The log says why: hardware_output is off, running on simulation time, can0 does not exist or the model has no hardware section.
symptoms.check: Search the MPC's start-up log for Hardware output. ros2 param get /talos/mpc_controller hardware_output; on the Orin ip -br link show can0.

symptoms.symptom: Talos moves weakly; thrusters never pass 500 RPM
symptoms.cause: table_mode was left on after a bench test. It caps every thruster at 500 RPM; the log says Table mode ON.
symptoms.check: ros2 param get /talos/mpc_controller table_mode, then ros2 param set /talos/mpc_controller table_mode false.

symptoms.symptom: MPC log: MPC solve … ms exceeds the control period
symptoms.cause: The solve took longer than the 50 ms tick. In a 20-minute pool session the median was 30 ms and the 95th percentile 35 ms, so this is unusual: something else is loading the Orin's CPU.
symptoms.check: ros2 topic echo /talos/controller/mpc/solve_time_ms; the CPU chip in the viewer's command bar; top on the Orin.

symptoms.symptom: Holding still, the MPC's learned disturbance sits at a constant few N·m
symptoms.cause: The model's statics (buoyancy, centre of buoyancy) are wrong. On 2026-10-26 a tethered identification run fitted the tether's pull into the statics; the next untethered run showed +2.7 N·m pitch, +0.7 N·m roll and +1.3 N heave of constant disturbance.
symptoms.check: Average controller/mpc/disturbance over a hold. Never take statics or added mass from a tethered run.

symptoms.symptom: The robot was enabled; opening the viewer killed it
symptoms.cause: Normal. From its first tick the viewer reports on slot 1, asserting kill until someone presses Enable.
symptoms.check: Press Enable in the viewer.

symptoms.symptom: Enable drops by itself: Another operator owns the enable switch
symptoms.cause: Something else published on slot 1 (a second viewer, the old RViz control panel, a script). The viewer yields at once and refuses Enable until that sender has been quiet for 1 s.
symptoms.check: ros2 topic info -v /talos/command/software_kill lists the publishers; ros2 topic echo /talos/command/software_kill --field sender_id names them.

symptoms.symptom: Talos stays enabled with nobody driving
symptoms.cause: A script cleared its slot with switch_asserting_kill: false, switch_needs_update: false. That latches: the slot stays clear forever. It happened on 2026-10-20 with a bench script releasing slot 3.
symptoms.check: Kill from the viewer (or pull the switch), then find the script. Scripts should hold slot 3 with needs_update: true, so they kill when they die.

symptoms.symptom: Killed, and no one pressed anything
symptoms.cause: A slot reporting with needs_update: true went quiet for 500 ms (its sender died or the link dropped), or the POAC board lost its micro-ROS connection: it is killed whenever it has none.
symptoms.check: ros2 topic echo /talos/state/firmware: kill_switches_timed_out and kill_switches_asserting_kill are bitmasks by slot.

symptoms.symptom: After set_camera_is_dfc, detections keep coming from the old camera, or stop for a while
symptoms.cause: The swap is asynchronous. The service answers "Successfully switched" at once; the detector reconfigures and loads the other model afterwards.
symptoms.check: Watch header.frame_id of /talos/detected_objects until it names the new camera. The pre-test tool allows up to 90 s.

symptoms.symptom: Holding up the torpedo board, detected_objects never says fire or blood
symptoms.cause: Expected. On the front camera the detector's torpedo task consumes the fire and blood detections and publishes torpedo plus fire_hole_large, fire_hole_small, blood_hole_large and blood_hole_small.
symptoms.check: ros2 topic echo /talos/detected_objects --field detections and read the class ids.

symptoms.symptom: You edited a config YAML and nothing changed
symptoms.cause: Nodes read the copy in install/<pkg>/share, not your source tree. Rebuild (or build with --symlink-install). On the robot, nothing changes until the code is deployed. (Building this site turned up a mapping prior that differed between the source and installed config.yaml.)
symptoms.check: ros2 pkg prefix riptide_mapping2, then diff that package's share/ config against src/. On a running node, ros2 param get.

symptoms.symptom: In sim, mapping's course offset starts hugely uncertain (about 17,900 m²)
symptoms.cause: A start-up bug: mapping stamps last_predict_time when the node starts, before /clock arrives, so the first drift prediction covers about 1.8 × 109 s (time zero to the sim clock). Only in sim; on the robot the clock is wall time.
symptoms.check: Echo /talos/mapping/<object> covariance right after start. A fix would start the first prediction at the first /clock message.

symptoms.symptom: The viewer loses TF (robot frozen, frames missing) right after a clock change
symptoms.cause: A clock that steps backwards by more than about 10 s makes the Nereus viewer drop TF. That is why the opbox time setup lets the robot step its clock only in its first three updates after boot.
symptoms.check: chronyc tracking on each machine. Restart the viewer after a big step.

symptoms.symptom: ros2 bag info fails: the bag folder has a .db3 but no metadata.yaml
symptoms.cause: The recorder was killed instead of stopped: metadata.yaml is written when it closes.
symptoms.check: ros2 bag reindex <bag folder> rebuilds it from the data. Stop recorders with Ctrl-C (the viewer's Stop does that).

symptoms.symptom: Playing a bag from the middle, TF can't connect the robot to the world
symptoms.cause: --start-offset skips everything before it, including /tf_static, where most static frames are published only once, at start-up (one is re-sent every 2 s).
symptoms.check: Re-publish the bag's statics with a static broadcaster (this chapter's static_tf_from_bag.py), or play from the start.

symptoms.symptom: A replay shows two of everything, or something on the robot reacts to it
symptoms.cause: The replay shares a graph with live nodes. Bag messages and live ones mix, and a replayed command could reach the robot.
symptoms.check: Isolate the replay: RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_fastrtps_cpp ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY=1 ROS_DOMAIN_ID=<unused> and unset the ZENOH_* variables.

symptoms.symptom: In a bag, messages seem to arrive before they were sent
symptoms.cause: The recorder's clock is behind the publisher's. A bench bag from 2026-10-27 has every message "arriving" about 37 ms early.
symptoms.check: chronyc tracking on both machines, or record on the Orin itself.

symptoms.symptom: git status says every behaviour tree changed after a check
symptoms.cause: checkBT re-saves every tree file in place (XML re-escaped, trailing newline dropped).
symptoms.check: Snapshot the trees folder before running it and restore afterwards, or git checkout the trees you didn't mean to change.
